parcalar.metin: [excited, emphatic science storyteller] Did you know? One of the world's most powerful wind turbines is rated at twenty-six megawatts!
On this Dongfang Electric test turbine in China, a single blade is one hundred fifty-three metres long. That's longer than a football pitch.
The rotor is three hundred ten metres across. Its blades sweep seventy-seven thousand square metres, about ten football pitches.
The five-megawatt reference turbine from our episode had a one-hundred-twenty-six-metre rotor. This giant is almost two and a half times wider.

[dramatic] The maker says that with an average wind of ten metres per second, it can generate one hundred million kilowatt-hours a year. That's the yearly electricity of about fifty-five thousand homes.
The giants of wind keep growing. Follow Kozmos Lab!
